articles.title: Endangered orangutans released back into the wild after Borneo fires
articles.summary: The critically endangered apes were rescued from intense wildfires that destroyed their habitat in August and September.
articles.body:
Eight orangutans have been released into the wild in Borneo after being rescued from intense wildfires.

Three mothers, their three daughters and two adult males were freed in a reserve in the west of the island on Friday.

Indonesian wildlife authorities rescued 46 of the apes, which are critically endangered, before fires tore through their habitat in August and September.

articles.title: After tragedy at Satya Niketan, 30 illegal, dangerous buildings razed daily
articles.summary: MCD demolishes 1,046 illegal properties in Delhi from Sept 6–Oct 10, sealing 282 and razing 47 dangerous buildings after Satya Niketan collapse.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) demolished at least 30 properties daily from Sept 6 to Oct 10 in a crackdown on illegal and dangerous buildings after the collapse of a paying guest accomodation in Satya Niketan killed seven people.According to govt data released Sunday, the corporation demolished 1,046 properties across its 12 zones, sealed 282 properties, and pulled down 47 dangerous buildings.Chief minister Rekha Gupta earlier directed MCD to intensify its demolition drive against illegal structures and dangerous buildings across all zones.Among the 12 zones, the maximum demolition action was recorded in Rohini (158 properties), followed by South (121) and Shahdara North (115). City-SP, West and Shahdara South zones saw action against 87 properties each, closely followed by Karol Bagh with 85. The remaining zones included Central, where action was taken against 75 properties; Civil Lines (63), Keshavpuram (61), Najafgarh (45) and Narela (62).Of the sealed properties, 87 were in City-SP zone, 41 in Shahdara North and South, 27 in Shahdara South, while 23 were in the Central zone.Karol Bagh accounted for 13 of the 47 dangerous buildings demolished. Civil Lines, City-SP and West zones reported eight each, while Narela, Rohini, Keshavpuram and South had two each. Shahdara South and Najafgarh reported one each.Following a building collapse in Seemapuri, one unsafe building was demolished and Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board issued notices to three other houses.Gupta said the campaign would continue, adding that agencies must act according to rules in cases involving illegal construction and unsafe buildings.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: CJP protest fallout: Delhi eases curbs, 20+ FIRs filed as Abhijeet Dipke-police row escalates
articles.summary: 20+ FIRs were filed after Delhi’s Jantar Mantar protest, with hundreds detained as demonstrations continued; police and activist Abhijeet Dipke traded claims over his detention.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A day after Delhi turned into a fortress to stop the protest against the SIR at Jantar Mantar, some restrictions were eased for commuters Sunday. Entry/exit at metro stations was reopened and interned in central Delhi restarted.However, multiple FIRs, detentions and fresh demonstrations continued.Police and Abhijeet Dipke also traded charges regarding when the CJP founder was informed about his grandmother’s death and the police’s conduct during his detention.Police sources said more than 20 FIRs were registered in connection with Saturday’s protest for alleged violations of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), for obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties, assaulting police personnel and other offences.While police sources put the number of protesters detained at 400, other accounts claimed that over 700 people had been detained.Protests and marches continued at several locations, including Connaught Place and RK Ashram Marg, with demonstrators demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police personnel remained deployed across sensitive areas to prevent gatherings and maintain law and order.In a relief to CJP’s three leading faces, an executive magistrate court ordered the release of Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were placed under preventive arrest after arriving in the capital Saturday. They were released after an undertaking that they would not cause any “breach of peace” for a year.Dipke later rejected claims that he had signed any agreement. He said the outfit would continue its demonstrations against the CEC.Dipke spoke to the media in Nagpur Sunday evening after arriving on a flight from New Delhi, before leaving by road in a car for his hometown in Hingoli district following the death of his grandmother.In Delhi, Dipke visited advocate Kapil Sibal’s house after being released by police. He alleged that after being detained at IGI Airport, he was not allowed to use his phone, contact his lawyer or speak to his cousin after learning about his grandmother’s death.“Delhi police woke me up at 3.30am today and asked me to call my parents and tell them that I had been arrested. My family is already mourning, and this would have been a bigger blow to them. It was very heartless behaviour,” he said.Delhi Police, meanwhile, released a video Sunday showing an officer informing Dipke about his grandmother’s death. A senior police officer said he had been informed around 2pm.In the video, the officer expressed condolences and offered to arrange for transport, including a bus or flight, if Dipke wished to attend the funeral. Dipke repeatedly responded, “I’ll stay,” when asked whether he wanted to leave.The officer also offered to facilitate a call with a family member through an official police number. When asked about speaking to his father, Dipke said he would not be able to speak to him.At one point, Dipke said, “Funeral kara do. Aaj hi kar do (Just arrange the funeral. Do it today).” The officer replied that the funeral had been scheduled for the following day and assured him that the police would try to facilitate any arrangements he needed.Dipke remained firm in his decision on not leaving. The officer told him he could inform the police if he changed his mind.In response to the video shared by the cops, Dipke posted on X: “Why did you delete the part where I was asking for my phone so I could retrieve my cousin’s number? And where I was asking to let me speak to my lawyers? The same Delhi Police, which is now taking the moral high ground for informing me about my grandmother’s demise and offering me a ride home, came to me at 3.30 in the morning with arrest papers, demanding that I sign them. Where did all that humanity go at 3.30am? Despite knowing that I had just lost my grandmother, they still insisted that I sign the arrest papers. articles.title: At least 72 Sudanese miners killed in air strike: Rights monitor
articles.summary: Emergency Lawyers blames Egypt for the deadly attack in northern Sudan.
articles.body:
An air raid at a gold mine near the disputed Sudan-Egypt border has killed at least 72 workers, according to a Sudanese rights group, after survivors described scenes of chaos in the mountainous region.

Emergency Lawyers, which documents atrocities in Sudan’s war, accused the Egyptian military of carrying out the attack.

“Egyptian fighter jets targeted civilian miners in the northern Wadi area inside Sudanese territory, resulting, according to preliminary information, in the killing of 72 civilians,” the Khartoum-based rights organisation wrote on X on Sunday.

The reported attack on Saturday cannot be independently verified, and Egypt has issued no official comment.

It was this year’s second attack on the mountainous border region of Jabal al-Uqaydat, a gold mining area. Similar strikes, also reportedly carried out by Egypt, killed 23 workers at the gold mining site in June.

The Egyptian military said at the time that it had conducted a “large-scale operation” against illegal gold mining within its borders.

The border between Sudan and Egypt is disputed, with both countries claiming the resource-rich Halaib Triangle.

Images shared on social media and by local rights groups, which could not be verified, showed dozens of bodies strewn in rubble and others wrapped in funeral shrouds. Miners described an air strike on the area.

Since April 2023, the war in Sudan between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has killed more than 200,000 people and created a humanitarian crisis that has pushed many into the dangerous gold mining industry, which fuels both sides’ war efforts.

The rugged mountainous area, home to bountiful mineral deposits, stretches for hundreds of kilometres and includes the disputed Halaib Triangle.

Emergency Lawyers said the attack occurred within Sudanese territory.

“The repeated attacks on the gold and mineral-rich border regions reflect a desire by Egyptian authorities to expand and assert control over Sudan’s natural resources,” it said.

The Egyptian army said in June that it carried out its operation “within Egyptian territory”.

It said 223 people were detained, including 136 foreign nationals, and announced a campaign to counter “illegal gold mining and arms smuggling” in the area.

Despite backing Sudan’s army chief, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, Egypt considers the war at its border – which stretches 1,200km (745 miles) from the Red Sea to Libya – a significant threat to its security.

East of the Nile River, the porous border has for years been a thriving conduit for gold, illicit trade and human trafficking, which Egypt has tried to stem, including by using mass deportations.

articles.title: UK weather: Remnants of hurricane Isaias to help bring warm weather this week
articles.summary: Close to record-breaking warm nights are possible this week as warmer air heads for the UK.
articles.body:
The remnants of Hurricane Isaias, which hit the southern US on Saturday, is set to bring a warm spell to the UK this week.

Close to record-breaking warm nights are possible, with Monday night temperatures for some parts of England possibly staying as high as 18C, not far off the country's October record of 18.6C (65.4F).

Daytime temperatures will be above average for the time of year for many parts of the UK.

Rain is likely at times across much of the UK, but will still fall below the amount required to help ease drought hit-parts of England .

Drought declared in Yorkshire after dry weather

North-westerly winds over the weekend meant it felt rather cool in many areas, but with southerly winds on Monday comes milder conditions to most parts. Temperatures will peak at 14 to 19 Celsius, slightly above the mid-October average of 12-16C.

However, weather fronts tied in with the southerly winds mean that most areas will be cloudy with occasional spells of rain or drizzle. Sunshine will be fairly limited with areas around north-east Scotland, east Wales, the West Midlands and the north coast of Northern Ireland most favoured for some sunny breaks.

A warm night will follow with temperatures only dropping a few degrees, but heavier bursts of rain are expected to develop through the night.

Overnight rain will then sweep across the UK through Tuesday morning. In the sunnier weather that follows, temperatures are likely to hit the low 20s in southern and eastern counties of England, with 23C possible in parts of East Anglia.

Windier midweek with another burst of warmth

Clearer skies into Wednesday morning mean all should experience a cooler start to the day, but a sunnier one too.

Cloud and strengthening winds will move into north-western parts during the afternoon, all linked to an area of low pressure passing between the UK and Iceland. which contains some of the remnants of ex-Hurricane Isaias.

Isaias hit the Florida coast on Saturday as a Category 2 storm, before weakening rapidly over land. As the resulting area of low pressure moves out into the Atlantic this week it will merge with another area of low pressure coming out of Canada before sweeping towards Iceland by the end of Wednesday.

Gales are expected for a time in the north-west of Scotland, and a narrow corridor of humid ex-tropical air will proceed an active cold front that will sweep a band of rain south-eastwards during Thursday and Thursday night.

Before the rain arrives in south-east England we could once again see temperatures exceed 20C in many locations on Thursday.

Following the passage of the wetter and windier weather, an area of high pressure will move in during Friday and this could hang around into the following week.

This will bring in cooler air again, dropping temperatures back to where they should be for the time of year and introducing chillier nights again.

High pressure also means rain amounts will be sparse which will be little comfort to those monitoring the ongoing drought. After a summer of extreme heat and little rain for most, some parts of the country have continued to experience below-average rainfall so far this autumn. While we are almost halfway through the season some parts of Yorkshire have seen less than 20% their normal autumn rainfall.

However, the Met Office continues to highlight the potential for late autumn and early winter being wetter than normal due to the record El Niño conditions this year.

articles.title: Nossa Senhora Aparecida: veja orações de proteção e agradecimento | G1
articles.standfirst: Rezas tradicionais da Igreja Católica incluem pedidos de amparo, consagração a Maria e orações feitas pelos papas Francisco e Bento XVI.
articles.summary: Reúna preces de proteção e a Consagração a Nossa Senhora Aparecida, com orações tradicionais e textos escritos pelos papas Francisco e Bento XVI.
articles.body:
Imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida — Foto: Thiago Leon/Santuário Nacional

O dia 12 de outubro é uma data de devoção para milhões de católicos brasileiros, que recorrem a Nossa Senhora Aparecida para agradecer por graças alcançadas, pedir proteção e fortalecer a fé.

Padroeira do Brasil, a Santa é homenageada com diferentes orações, transmitidas entre gerações e presentes nas celebrações religiosas. Entre elas estão o tradicional Salve, Rainha, a Consagração à Nossa Senhora Aparecida e uma prece dedicada à proteção dos fiéis.

Com a chegada do feriado religioso, o g1 reuniu seis orações para quem deseja homenagear a Padroeira. Confira os textos das preces abaixo!

O Salve, Rainha é uma oração tradicional da Igreja Católica, frequentemente rezada ao final das contemplações do Santo Rosário. A prece invoca Maria como mãe de misericórdia e pede sua intercessão junto a Jesus.

"Infinitas graças vos damos, soberana Rainha, pelos benefícios que todos os dias recebemos de vossas mãos liberais. Dignai-vos agora e para sempre tomar-nos debaixo de vosso poderoso amparo, e para mais vos obrigar, vos saudamos com um Salve, Rainha.

Salve, Rainha, Mãe de misericórdia, vida, doçura e esperança nossa, salve! A vós bradamos, os degredados filhos de Eva; a vós suspiramos, gemendo e chorando neste vale de lágrimas. Eia, pois, Advogada nossa, esses vossos olhos misericordiosos a nós volvei e depois deste desterro mostrai-nos Jesus, bendito fruto do vosso ventre, ó, clemente, ó, piedosa, ó, doce Virgem Maria! Rogai por nós, Santa Mãe de Deus, para que sejamos dignos das promessas de Cristo. Amém".

A Consagração à Nossa Senhora Aparecida é uma das orações mais conhecidas entre os devotos. O texto foi modificado pelo Papa Francisco durante sua visita a Aparecida, em 2013.

Na prece, os fiéis consagram a Maria seus pensamentos, palavras e coração, além de pedir acolhimento e proteção.

"Ó Maria Santíssima, pelos méritos de Nosso Senhor Jesus Cristo, em vossa querida imagem de Aparecida, espalhais inúmeros benefícios sobre todo o Brasil.

Eu, embora indigno de pertencer ao número de vossos filhos e filhas, mas cheio do desejo de participar dos benefícios de vossa misericórdia, prostrado a vossos pés, consagro-vos o meu entendimento, para que sempre pense no amor que mereceis; consagro-vos a minha língua para que sempre vos louve e propague a vossa devoção; consagro-vos o meu coração, para que, depois de Deus, vos ame sobre todas as coisas.

Recebei-me, ó Rainha incomparável, vós que o Cristo crucificado deu-nos por Mãe, no ditoso número de vossos filhos e filhas; acolhei-me debaixo de vossa proteção; socorrei-me em todas as minhas necessidades, espirituais e temporais, sobretudo na hora de minha morte.

Abençoai-me, ó celestial cooperadora, e com vossa poderosa intercessão, fortalecei-me em minha fraqueza, a fim de que, servindo-vos fielmente nesta vida, possa louvar-vos, amar-vos e dar-vos graças no céu, por toda eternidade. Assim seja!"

Terço dos Homens em Aparecida, em 2026. — Foto: Thiago Leon/A12

Oração de Nossa Senhora Aparecida para proteção

Presente no Manual do Devoto desde 1904, a oração é rezada após a Consagração à Nossa Senhora Aparecida durante as novenas. A prece é uma forma de pedir proteção diante das dificuldades e de confiar à Santa intenções particulares.

"Ó incomparável Senhora da Conceição Aparecida. Mãe de Deus, Rainha dos Anjos, Advogada dos pecadores, refúgio e consolação dos aflitos e atribulados, Virgem Santíssima cheia de poder e de bondade, lançai sobre nós um olhar favorável, para que sejamos socorridos por vós, em todas as necessidades em que nos acharmos.

Lembrai-vos, ó clementíssima Mãe Aparecida, que nunca se ouviu dizer que algum daqueles que têm a vós recorrido, invocado vosso santíssimo nome e implorado vossa singular proteção, fosse por vós abandonado. Animados com esta confiança, a vós recorremos.

Tomamo-nos de hoje para sempre por nossa Mãe, nossa protetora, consolação e guia, esperança e luz na hora da morte. Livrai-nos de tudo o que possa ofender-vos e a vosso Santíssimo Filho, Jesus.

Preservai-nos de todos os perigos da alma e do corpo; dirigi-nos em todos os negócios espirituais e temporais. Livrai-nos da tentação do demônio, para que, trilhando o caminho da virtude, possamos um dia ver-vos e amar-vos na eterna glória, por todos os séculos dos séculos. Amém".

Oração de Nossa Senhora Aparecida rezada pelo Papa Francisco

Durante sua visita ao Brasil, o Papa Francisco rezou diante da imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida. A oração fala sobre a missão cristã, a confiança em Deus e o pedido de acompanhamento e amparo de Maria.

"Mãe Aparecida, como Vós um dia, assim me sinto hoje diante do vosso e meu Deus, que nos propõe para a vida uma missão cujos contornos e limites desconhecemos, cujas exigências apenas vislumbramos. Mas, em vossa fé de que 'para Deus nada é impossível', Vós, ó Mãe, não hesitastes, e eu não posso hesitar. Assim, ó Mãe, como Vós, Eu abraço minha missão. Em vossas mãos coloco minha vida e vamos Vós-Mãe e Eu-Filho caminhar juntos, crer juntos, lutar juntos, vencer juntos como sempre juntos caminhastes vosso Filho e Vós.

Mãe Aparecida, um dia levastes vosso Filho ao templo para O consagrar ao Pai, para que fosse inteira disponibilidade para a missão. Levai-me hoje ao mesmo Pai, consagrai-me a Ele com tudo o que sou e com tudo o que tenho. Mãe Aparecida, ponho em vossas mãos, e levai até o Pai a nossa e vossa juventude, a Jornada Mundial da Juventude: quanta força, quanta vida, quanto dinamismo brotando e explodindo e que podem estar a serviço da vida, da humanidade.

Finalmente, ó Mãe, vos pedimos: permanecei aqui, sempre acolhendo vossos filhos e filhas peregrinos, mas também ide conosco, estai sempre ao nosso lado e acompanhai na missão e grande família dos devotos, principalmente quando a cruz mais nos pesar, sustentai nossa esperança de nossa fé".

Imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, Padroeira do Brasil — Foto: Arquivo/Thiago Leon/Santuário Nacional de Aparecida

A Oração Jubilar foi criada para as comemorações dos 300 anos do encontro da imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, em 2017. A prece recorda a história da devoção, agradece pelas graças recebidas e pede que os fiéis vivam a fé com gratidão e fidelidade.

"Senhora Aparecida, Mãe Padroeira, em vossa singela imagem. Há 300 anos aparecestes nas redes dos três benditos pescadores no Rio Paraíba do Sul. Como sinal vindo do céu, em vossa cor, vós nos dizeis que para o Pai não existem escravos, apenas filhos muito amados. Diante de vós, embaixadora de Deus, rompem-se as correntes da escravidão!

Assim, daquelas redes, passastes para o coração e a vida de milhões de outros filhos e filhas vossos. Para todos tendes sido bênção: peixes em abundância, famílias recuperadas, saúde alcançada, corações reconciliados, vida cristã reassumida. Nós vos agradecemos tanto carinho, tanto cuidado!

Hoje, em vosso Santuário e em vossa visita peregrina, nós vos acolhemos como mãe, e de vossas mãos recebemos o fruto de vossa missão entre nós: o vosso Filho Jesus, nosso Salvador. Recordai-nos o poder, a força das mãos postas em prece! Ensinai-nos a viver vosso jubileu com gratidão e fidelidade!

Fazei de nós vossos filhos e filhas, irmãos e irmãs de nosso Irmão Primogênito, Jesus Cristo. Amém!"

Durante a visita ao Brasil, em 2007, o Papa Bento XVI também rezou uma oração dedicada a Nossa Senhora Aparecida. A prece pede proteção para as famílias brasileiras e latino-americanas, além de paz, prosperidade e fortalecimento da fé.

"Mãe nossa, protegei a família brasileira e latino-americana!

Amparai, sob o vosso manto protetor, os filhos dessa Pátria querida que nos acolhe.

Vós que sois a Advogada junto ao vosso Filho Jesus, dai ao Povo brasileiro paz constante e prosperidade completa.

Concedei aos nossos irmãos de toda a geografia latino-americana um verdadeiro ardor missionário irradiador de fé e de esperança.

Fazei que o vosso clamor de Fátima pela conversão dos pecadores seja realidade, e transforme a vida da nossa sociedade.

E vós que, do Santuário de Guadalupe, intercedeis pelo povo do Continente da esperança, abençoai as suas terras e os seus lares. Amém".

articles.title: A nova onda de protestos de jovens do movimento das 'baratas' na Índia em imagens | G1
articles.standfirst: Movimento político satírico liderado pela Geração Z indiana voltou às ruas neste fim de semana para exigir a renúncia da principal autoridade eleitoral do país.
articles.summary: Movimento político satírico liderado pela Geração Z indiana voltou às ruas neste fim de semana para exigir a renúncia da principal autoridade eleitoral do país.
articles.body:
Um manifestante grita palavras de ordem de dentro de uma viatura policial após ser detido durante protesto em Mumbai — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

Em uma nova onda de protestos na Índia, o movimento Partido do Povo Barata (CJP, na sigla em inglês para Cockroach Janta Party ) levou milhares de jovens às ruas de Mumbai e Nova Déli neste fim de semana para pedir a renúncia da principal autoridade eleitoral do país.

O CJP é um movimento político satírico liderado pela Geração Z indiana que surgiu a partir de declarações feitas em maio pelo presidente do Supremo Tribunal da Índia, que usou o termo "barata" para descrever jovens desempregados que se dedicam ao jornalismo e ao ativismo.

Após a repercussão negativa dos comentários, o presidente da Corte disse que se referia apenas àqueles com "diplomas falsos e fraudulentos".

Na época, jovens vinham organizando manifestações para exigir reformas na educação e a renúncia do então ministro da Educação, o que acabou acontecendo em julho.

Desta vez, o CJP — que não está registrado como partido político na Índia — busca reformas eleitorais a poucos meses da realização de eleições estaduais consideradas cruciais para o país.

Os jovens também pedem a renúncia do Comissário-Chefe da Comissão Eleitoral, Gyanesh Kumar, sob alegações de manipulação das listas de eleitores — o que a Comissão Eleitoral rechaça.

Juntamente com partidos de oposição, eles afirmam que o processo de atualização da lista de eleitores é tendencioso — acusação negada tanto pela Comissão Eleitoral quanto pelo governo, que descreve a iniciativa como um esforço de rotina para remover eleitores falecidos, duplicados ou inelegíveis.

Polícia deteve Neha Bora, uma das figuras de destaque do protesto e presidente da associação da estudantes da Índia (AISA), durante uma manifestação em Déli no domingo — Foto: Reuters via BBC

Milhares de agentes de segurança foram deslocados para os locais das manifestações e estradas foram bloqueadas por barricadas.

A imprensa local relata que 7.000 manifestantes foram detidos e liberados no sábado (10/10) e que outras centenas de detenções ocorreram no domingo (11/10).

Abhijeet Dipke, que deu início ao movimento em maio, e outros líderes foram detidos ao chegarem a Nova Déli no sábado e soltos na manhã de domingo por um tribunal de primeira instância "sob a condição de que não perturbem a ordem pública pelo período de um ano", segundo informou a polícia.

Em seus primeiros comentários após ser liberado, Dipke afirmou que "o CJP não recuará nem se deixará intimidar".

E publicou no X: "[Narendra] Modi, como primeiro-ministro, é uma vergonha para a Índia."

Abhijeet Dipke, fundador do CJP, após ser liberado pela polícia. Ele e outros líderes de destaque do movimento foram retirados de um avião por agentes ao chegarem a Déli no sábado, mas foram liberados no dia seguinte — Foto: Reuters via BBC

Efetivos da Força de Ação Rápida, juntamente com policiais, foram mobilizados após o CJP anunciar a realização dos protestos — Foto: Reuters via BBC

Relatos da imprensa indicam que cerca de 7.000 pessoas foram detidas em Déli no sábado — Foto: Reuters via BBC

Manifestantes se posicionaram diante das viaturas policiais para impedir que levassem os detidos — Foto: Reuters via BBC

articles.title: Cadastro Digital de eventos para 2027 já está disponível | G1
articles.standfirst: O levantamento antecipado permite identificar possíveis conflitos de datas.
articles.summary: O levantamento antecipado permite identificar possíveis conflitos de datas.
articles.body:
Produtores podem enviar propostas pela plataforma Colab e acompanhar a análise dos órgãos municipais envolvidos — Foto: Divulgação

Já está disponível na plataforma digital Colab, dentro Projeto Rio das Ostras Digital, o cadastro de eventos previstos para 2027 no Município. A ferramenta permite que produtores, empresas, associações, instituições, entidades religiosas, órgãos públicos e outros interessados apresentem propostas à Prefeitura, informem as características das atividades, anexem documentos e solicitem análise para utilização de espaços públicos.

A iniciativa é coordenada pela Secretaria Municipal de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Turismo e tem como objetivo reunir informações antecipadas para organizar o calendário municipal e planejar os serviços necessários para cada evento.

Por meio do Cadastro Integrado e Solicitação de Análise de Eventos, o organizador também pode indicar eventuais apoios que pretende solicitar ao Município e acompanhar pela plataforma as manifestações dos órgãos municipais envolvidos no processo.

As informações cadastradas serão utilizadas no planejamento do Calendário Municipal de Eventos. O levantamento antecipado permite identificar possíveis conflitos de datas e locais e organizar, conforme a necessidade de cada atividade, ações relacionadas a Turismo, Trânsito, Segurança, Saúde, Meio Ambiente, limpeza urbana e Desenvolvimento Econômico.

“Queremos conhecer as propostas para 2027 desde já. Quando o Município dispõe dessas informações com antecedência, consegue dialogar melhor com os organizadores, planejar a atuação das secretarias e avaliar o potencial de cada evento para movimentar a Cidade”, explica o secretário de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Turismo, Pablo Kling.

O cadastro e a solicitação de análise não representam autorização automática para a realização do evento e nem garantem apoio do Poder Público. É importante ressaltar que, quando houver necessidade de alvará ou outras licenças, o responsável deverá cumprir os procedimentos e os prazos estabelecidos pela legislação. Esses procedimentos também podem ser acompanhados pela plataforma, conforme o serviço solicitado.

COMO CADASTRAR UM EVENTO – Para cadastrar um evento, o organizador deve acessar a opção Autorização de Eventos no Portal de Serviços Digitais da Prefeitura de Rio das Ostras. Depois de ler as informações sobre o serviço, é necessário clicar em “Próximo” e fazer a autenticação solicitada pela plataforma.

Em seguida, o responsável deve preencher os dados do evento, informar eventuais apoios pretendidos, anexar os documentos necessários e revisar as informações antes de enviar a solicitação para análise.

articles.title: De salão de 4 cadeiras a complexo de beleza com 188 colaboradores | G1
articles.standfirst: Laiane Granieri começou como maquiadora e transformou o negócio em uma operação com 48 pontos de atendimento e projeção de faturamento de R$ 5 milhões em 2026.
articles.summary: Laiane Granieri começou como maquiadora e transformou o negócio em uma operação com 48 pontos de atendimento e projeção de faturamento de R$ 5 milhões em 2026.
articles.body:
Quando abriu seu primeiro espaço de beleza em São Paulo , Laiane Granieri tinha apenas quatro cadeiras e um objetivo claro : oferecer uma experiência mais conveniente para as clientes .

Hoje, a empresária comanda um complexo de beleza com 48 pontos de atendimento, cerca de 188 colaboradores e serviços que vão de salão e spa a barbearia e atendimento externo para eventos.

A história da empreendedora começou cedo. Aos 18 anos, ela trabalhava com o pai vendendo roupas na região da Rua 25 de Março, tradicional polo comercial da capital paulista.

Mais tarde, decidiu seguir sua paixão pelo universo da beleza, atuando primeiro como maquiadora e, depois, como cabeleireira. Foi dessa experiência que nasceu a ideia do próprio negócio.

O principal diferencial da empresa é o atendimento sem hora marcada. A inspiração veio de uma dor vivida pela própria fundadora, que frequentemente precisava reorganizar a rotina para cumprir horários agendados em salões de beleza.

A proposta encontrou espaço em um mercado que valoriza cada vez mais praticidade e flexibilidade. Ao longo dos anos, o negócio deixou de ser apenas um salão para se tornar um ecossistema de beleza.

Além dos serviços tradicionais de cabelo e maquiagem, o espaço reúne coloração, terapia capilar, barbearia, spa e atendimento especializado para casamentos, shows e outras ocasiões.

De salão de 4 cadeiras a complexo de beleza com 188 colaboradores — Foto: Reprodução/PEGN

A estratégia é concentrar diferentes necessidades em um único local, ampliando o ticket médio e a conveniência para os clientes.

O crescimento aconteceu em etapas. Em 2023, a empresa operava com dez cadeiras. A cada nova expansão, Laiane Granieri incorporava espaços vizinhos e adicionava novos serviços. O resultado foi a criação de uma estrutura formada por mais de quatro lojas integradas.

Para manter a operação funcionando diariamente, a empresária aposta na gestão de pessoas. O negócio trabalha em diferentes escalas de atendimento, das 8h às 20h , e todos os novos colaboradores passam por treinamentos focados na cultura da empresa e no acolhimento ao cliente.

A empreendedora afirma que o atendimento é o principal ativo do negócio . Ouvir críticas, acompanhar a experiência das clientes e manter o padrão de serviço foram práticas que ajudaram a sustentar a expansão acelerada.

A operação também enfrentou desafios típicos do crescimento. Entre os erros cometidos no início da trajetória, ela cita o excesso de estoque e a dificuldade para dimensionar corretamente a demanda .

Com o tempo, passou a utilizar indicadores de atendimento e consumo para ajustar compras e reduzir desperdícios.

Os números mostram a evolução do empreendimento. Se no começo a comemoração vinha após atender dez clientes em um dia, hoje o salão chega a receber centenas de pessoas em datas de grande movimento.

Em um dos períodos mais intensos, a operação registrou atendimento de 358 clientes em um único dia .

Agora, a empresária prepara a inauguração da primeira unidade fora da sede original, na Vila Prudente, zona leste de São Paulo.

O projeto faz parte de um plano ainda mais ambicioso: transformar a marca em uma rede de abrangência nacional e, futuramente, internacional, possivelmente por meio do modelo de franquias.

Para quem deseja empreender no segmento de beleza, Laiane Granieri deixa um conselho simples: consistência.

Segundo ela, o crescimento do negócio foi resultado de pequenas ações repetidas diariamente ao longo dos anos. "Você vai plantando uma sementinha todos os dias. Mas a colheita é maravilhosa", afirma.

articles.title: Menino de 12 anos é especialista em elevadores e escadas rolantes | G1
articles.standfirst: Alex Turini mora no DF e desenvolveu fascínio pelas máquinas; hoje, é figura conhecida das empresas de manutenção. Vídeo no Aeroporto JK ultrapassou 15 mil curtidas.
articles.summary: O menino especialista em elevadores Alex Turini mostra seus conhecimentos técnicos e conta como a paixão pelas máquinas começou após ficar preso em uma delas.
articles.body:
Para quem mora em cidade grande, pegar um elevador ou uma escada rolante é uma atividade como qualquer outra – um jeito de subir ou descer os andares. Mas para o brasiliense Alex Turini, de 12 anos, eles são muito mais que isso: são um universo cheio de possibilidades e engrenagens para entender. ⚙️💭🔧

Em um passeio no shopping com o g1 , ele mostrou seus vastos conhecimentos sobre esses meios de locomoção (veja vídeo acima) .

Alex conta que sua paixão começou depois que ele ficou preso em um elevador pela primeira vez. Ao invés de um trauma, o que surgiu foi a curiosidade de saber como aquele equipamento funcionava.

De tanto investigar, chegou a ficar preso mais 17 vezes (😱), sem qualquer susto ou medo. Pelo contrário: a cada "prisão", ele se interessava mais.

O molho de chaves que Alex guarda no bolso e leva para quase todos os lugares é especial. Nele, estão todas as chaves para ligar elevadores e escadas que ele acumulou em suas visitas a salas de máquina — espaços onde estão os equipamentos para controlar os sistemas que operam essas instalações.

"Se eu perco isso aqui [molho de chaves], eu choro por 15 dias", brinca Alex. "São as chaves que eu coleciono, separo elas por empresas."

O brasiliense Alex Turini, de 12 anos, é fascinado por escadas e elevadores — Foto: Bruna Yamaguti/G1

Alex e sua família moram em apartamento. Ele conta que, sempre que alguém fica preso no elevador do prédio, é para ele que o porteiro liga.

"Teve uma vez que um cara ficou preso e o porteiro era novo, não sabia mexer no elevador. Tinha que fazer uma manobra e eu sabia fazer. Aí ele me ligou, eu já coloquei meu capacete, cinto e luva, liguei pra empresa do elevador e tirei o cara de lá. Ele me abraçou e agradeceu umas 100 vezes", lembra Alex.

A paixão pelo funcionamento dessas máquina já deu a Alex a certeza da profissão que quer seguir quando for adulto: engenheiro mecânico.

"Quero trabalhar primeiro como técnico, e depois ser engenheiro", diz o menino.

Alex Turini ganhou visita aos bastidores do Aeroporto de Brasília — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

A curiosidade envolve toda a família. Alex contou ao g1 que já foi levado pela mãe ao Aeroporto de Brasília , em plena madrugada, para matar uma curiosidade: como funcionavam as escadas e elevadores do terminal depois da meia-noite?

Nessa empreitada, Alex teve a oportunidade de conhecer a equipe de manutenção do Aeroporto de Brasília. E a amizade gerou um vídeo para as redes sociais do terminal, com os bastidores dos equipamentos.

Até esse fim de semana, o conteúdo já tinha viralizado e reunido mais de 15 mil curtidas nas redes sociais.

"Ele gosta tanto desse universo que passou a acompanhar as manutenções desses equipamentos e até ganhou um apelido: Mike Tanguinho. O nome vem de Mike Tango (MT), como chamamos o time de Manutenção por aqui", diz a publicação do Aeroporto de Brasília.

articles.title: Trent Park: A mansão que espionou generais nazistas na 2ª Guerra | G1
articles.standfirst: Enquanto oficiais nazistas de alta patente capturados como prisioneiros de guerra conversavam à vontade nas elegantes salas de Trent Park, seus diálogos eram ouvidos às escondidas no porão por agentes britânicos.
articles.summary: A mansão Trent Park utilizou escutas escondidas para obter dados cruciais sobre armas e atrocidades de generais nazistas durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial.
articles.body:
A mansão inglesa onde os britânicos levaram nazistas a revelar seus segredos — Foto: HOUGHTON HALL

A Casa dos Segredos de Trent Park faz jus ao nome. A fachada e os salões do térreo dessa elegante mansão no norte de Londres revelam o gosto refinado de sir Philip Sassoon, esteta e grande anfitrião antes da guerra. Mas quem desce ao porão encontra uma história pouco conhecida de espionagem e intrigas durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial (1939-1945).

Aviso: este artigo menciona o Holocausto e pode causar desconforto em alguns leitores.

No mês passado, Trent Park abriu as portas ao público pela primeira vez como museu, em reconhecimento a seu papel crucial durante a guerra.

Foi ali que uma equipe monitorou, às escondidas, as conversas de prisioneiros de guerra alemães de alta patente mantidos na mansão. Muitos dos agentes eram refugiados judeus alemães. Os generais nazistas não faziam ideia de que cada palavra sua era captada por microfones. Convencidos de que estavam seguros, deixaram escapar informações vitais que mudaram o curso da guerra.

O político e colecionador de arte sir Philip Sassoon herdou Trent Park em 1912. Na década de 1920, promoveu uma grande remodelação da fachada e dos interiores, seguindo o estilo neogeorgiano, então muito em voga.

O luxo dos salões, onde havia microfones escondidos, ajudou a fazer os generais nazistas se sentirem seguros — Foto: James O Davies

"A arquitetura que ele criou é muito elegante, serena e discreta. Os interiores seguem a mesma linha: sem excessos, muito amplos e com poucas antiguidades, todas belíssimas e de grande valor", disse Simon Thurley, assessor sênior de Trent Park, à BBC.

Papéis de parede chineses requintados e retratos da família pintados pelo pintor húngaro Philip de László e pelo italiano John Singer Sargent decoram as paredes.

Os interiores do térreo dessa elegante mansão foram agora recriados com todo o cuidado.

"As pessoas vão sentir que voltaram ao mundo de Sassoon quando estiverem aqui", diz Giuseppe Albano, diretor do museu. "Mas, depois, é claro, elas descem."

O porão é, de fato, outra história. Sir Philip morreu em junho de 1939 e, quando a guerra começou, em setembro, o governo britânico requisitou a mansão. Thomas Kendrick, um dos mais altos dirigentes do serviço secreto britânico, identificou o local como ideal para instalar um Centro de Interrogatório Detalhado dos Serviços Combinados (CSDIC, na sigla em inglês).

Um retrato de Sybil, marquesa de Cholmondeley e irmã do proprietário, pintado por John Singer Sargent, é uma das obras de destaque da mansão — Foto: James O Davies

Kendrick já havia testado a escuta de prisioneiros de guerra na Tower of London (Torre de Londres), mas percebeu que os centros de interrogatório precisavam funcionar em locais mais discretos e afastados o bastante do centro da capital para reduzir o risco de bombardeios.

No porão da mansão, um sistema de gravação registrou as conversas privadas dos generais nazistas — Foto: Trent Park Museum Trust

Trent Park, Latimer House e Wilton Park também tinham o espaço necessário para que Kendrick ampliasse a operação e obtivesse, em conversas privadas dos prisioneiros, as informações que buscava.

"A mansão inteira e o bloco das cocheiras foram equipados com microfones", disse a historiadora Helen Fry, autora de The Walls Have Ears ("as paredes têm ouvidos", em tradução literal) à BBC.

Havia microfones escondidos em vasos de plantas, luminárias e na mesa de bilhar, além de árvores nos jardins.

Fios ocultos, instalados atrás dos painéis e sob o assoalho, ligavam esses microfones às salas equipadas para a escuta no porão, conhecidas como salas "M" e recriadas pelo museu.

De lá, agentes de escuta — inicialmente britânicos que falavam alemão — monitoravam as conversas dia e noite.

Trent Park se tornaria o principal centro de detenção de oficiais alemães de alta patente, muitos deles de famílias ricas ou aristocráticas. A presunção de que tinham direito a tratamento privilegiado parece ter feito deles presas surpreendentemente fáceis para os planos de Kendrick.

Os parentes de Sassoon talvez tenham levado as valiosas antiguidades da mansão, substituídas por móveis do governo, bem mais funcionais. Ainda assim, a casa continuava sendo uma prisão luxuosa, pensada para fazer os detidos baixarem a guarda.

Cada general tinha seu próprio criado militar, também capturado com ele. Havia uma biblioteca, oficiais britânicos davam aulas de inglês e, de vez em quando, os prisioneiros podiam até sair para passear pela cidade.

Os prisioneiros também tinham um responsável por seu bem-estar: o fictício lorde Aberfeldy, aristocrata escocês interpretado por um jovem oficial de interrogatório.

"Ele recebeu o nome de uma destilaria de uísque", brinca Fry.

Aberfeldy dizia admirar Adolf Hitler (1889-1945) em segredo e visitava os prisioneiros para levá-los a fazer confidências que, é claro, eram captadas pelos agentes de escuta no porão.

Nos jardins, os aparelhos de gravação foram escondidos entre as plantas e atrás das árvores — Foto: Houghton Hall

Todos os oficiais alemães eram avisados de que, se fossem capturados, suas conversas poderiam ser monitoradas. Ainda assim, os generais parecem ter acreditado, para surpresa de todos, que isso não acontecia em Trent Park.

"Há uma gravação impressionante de dois generais conversando sobre o assunto. Eles dizem: 'Bem, fomos avisados, mas é claro que não estão nos monitorando. Perceberíamos se estivessem'", conta Thurley, o assessor, rindo.

"Você massageia o ego deles, alimenta a sensação de importância, e eles deixam de pensar com lógica", diz Fry.

As informações continuavam a chegar com regularidade, mas, com o avanço da guerra, ficou claro que os agentes britânicos tinham dificuldade para entender o jargão e as gírias. Eles haviam aprendido alemão apenas em contexto acadêmico.

Por isso, decidiu-se recrutar refugiados judeus que falavam alemão, vindos da Alemanha, da Áustria e da Tchecoslováquia.

Um desses recrutas foi Ernst Lederer, avô da comediante e atriz Helen Lederer. Em 1939, ele fugiu da Tchecoslováquia em um dos últimos trens a deixar o país.

Como os demais agentes de escuta, assinou a Lei de Segredos Oficiais e manteve segredo sobre seu trabalho durante a guerra até o fim da vida.

Ernst Lederer foi um dos agentes que ouviam secretamente as conversas dos prisioneiros — Foto: Houghton Hall

"A mulher dele achava que ele fazia parte da Home Guard, a força britânica de defesa local. Na verdade, ele ia cumprir longos turnos em Trent Park", disse à BBC a neta de Lederer, que hoje trabalha no roteiro de um filme sobre o que aconteceu lá.

"Não sabíamos o que ele fazia até que, por acaso, participei de um documentário chamado War Hero in My Family ("um herói de guerra na minha família", em tradução literal), do Channel 5."

A série acompanhava personalidades que investigavam documentos secretos sobre a atuação de seus pais e avós durante a guerra.

"E há um detalhe inusitado: minha mãe, que era inglesa, foi convocada para trabalhar em Bletchley Park aos 21 anos", diz Lederer.

"Ela costumava participar de passeios em família com Ernst Lederer, e nenhum dos dois sabia o que o outro havia feito."

De fato, os agentes de escuta não sabiam da existência do Centro de decifração de códigos de Bletchley Park, embora seus superiores soubessem. Informações foram compartilhadas entre os dois locais durante toda a guerra.

Em 1941, agentes de Trent Park ouviram uma conversa que mencionava o Knickebein ("perna torta", em tradução livre), um sistema de orientação por feixes que permitia aos bombardeiros noturnos atingir com precisão fábricas britânicas de munições. Os decifradores de códigos de Bletchley Park confirmaram a informação e repassaram ao serviço de inteligência da Força Aérea os dados necessários para interferir nos sinais.

O general Wilhelm Ritter von Thoma foi gravado conversando com outro prisioneiro, o general Ludwig Crüwell, sobre o programa secreto nazista de 'armas de retaliação'. Entre elas estavam as bombas voadoras V1, movidas por motores a jato pulsante, e os foguetes V2, que usavam oxigênio líquido como combustível — Foto: Getty Images

A informação mais importante obtida em Trent Park dizia respeito, sem dúvida, ao programa secreto alemão das armas V. O projeto previa desenvolver as poderosas Vergeltungswaffen (armas de vingança, em tradução livre), destinadas a ser lançadas contra cidades aliadas, como Londres.

Uma conversa captada mencionou um foguete capaz de atingir 15 km de altitude; outra revelou a existência do V-2, o primeiro míssil balístico de longo alcance do mundo, com alcance de 300 km.

As informações acabaram levando ao bombardeio, em agosto de 1943, do principal centro alemão de pesquisa e testes de foguetes e mísseis, em Peenemünde, na costa do mar Báltico. Como ressalta Fry em seu livro, o impacto do ataque foi imenso.

O primeiro ataque com um foguete V-1 contra Londres foi adiado para 13 de junho de 1944, uma semana depois do desembarque aliado na Normandia, no Dia D. Se os V-1 tivessem sido lançados antes, é possível que o desembarque nem tivesse ocorrido. O primeiro V-2 só caiu em Londres em 8 de setembro de 1944.

A equipe da mansão Trent Park também obteve "informações sobre a dimensão das atrocidades que Hitler vinha cometendo, pouco conhecidas na época", diz Albano, diretor do Museu. Para ouvintes judeus como Eric Mark, escutar essas conversas deve ter sido extremamente traumático: os pais dele foram mortos nas câmaras de gás de Treblinka, em 1943.

Mark, que morreu em 2020, contou que ouvia os alemães se gabarem do que haviam feito. "Diziam coisas como: 'Despachei [matei] uns 1.500'."

A casa hoje funciona como museu aberto ao público, o Trent Park House of Secrets — Foto: Ruth Board

Essas informações nunca foram usadas em julgamentos por crimes de guerra, pois isso exigiria revelar como haviam sido obtidas. "O governo britânico da época não queria que as táticas, a tecnologia ou a audácia da operação se tornassem conhecidas, sobretudo diante da perspectiva de uma Guerra Fria com a Rússia", explica Albano.

É difícil aceitar que pessoas que, na prática, confessaram ter cometido atrocidades tenham escapado da Justiça. Na época, o governo britânico estava muito preocupado com a dimensão da ameaça russa, em grande parte por causa das conversas interceptadas em Trent Park.

O local só encerrou as atividades de escuta em novembro de 1945.

"Trent Park e os outros dois centros da rede nos prepararam para a Guerra Fria de maneiras que ninguém percebeu, ou compreendeu de fato até agora", diz Fry.

"Seu legado é imensurável, e só agora começamos a compreender sua dimensão."

articles.title: Iran’s FM urges diplomacy in call with Saudi counterpart
articles.summary: Tehran offers to facilitate talks between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis following deadly strikes on the kingdom.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabian Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud has received a phone call from his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, the Saudi state news agency reported.

The two ministers discussed the recent escalations in the region after the Houthis, backed by Iran, attacked Saudi airports.

In a post on Telegram on Sunday, Araghchi emphasised that insisting on a military approach while disregarding political solutions would further complicate the situation. The Iranian minister said the region’s crises have no military solutions. Last week, Araghchi said “there is no military solution” to the US war, adding, “only negotiations based on justice and fairness” could end the conflict.

Araghchi said Iran is ready to provide any assistance necessary to facilitate the start of dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen and to help achieve a political solution.

Following the deadly attack on the Riyadh airport that killed 12 people and wounded 300, US President Donald Trump said he would reconsider the US role in Yemen, adding that he is weighing resuming strikes on Iran.

These remarks represent a departure from the president’s comments on Thursday that Washington will not resume strikes on Iran until after the US midterm elections.

Iranian and Saudi diplomatic ties have endured despite longstanding friction, with embassies restored under a 2023 Chinese-brokered agreement remaining operational. Before that breakthrough, a seven-year diplomatic rupture had fuelled regional proxy conflicts.

Riyadh’s relationship with Tehran has deteriorated since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran in late February. Following the attacks, Tehran and its aligned forces have struck US military assets and energy infrastructure across the Gulf region, including oil fields in Saudi Arabia.

In March 2026, Prince Faisal warned Iran that tolerance of its attacks on Saudi Arabia and those of neighbouring Gulf states is limited, calling on Tehran to “recalculate” its strategy.

articles.title: 'Started to sink backwards': 139 migrants, including 15 children, killed as boat capsizes off Djibouti
articles.summary: At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, have died and 84 remain missing after an overcrowded boat capsized off the coast of Djibouti while carrying
articles.body: At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, have died and 84 remain missing after an overcrowded boat capsized off the coast of Djibouti while carrying more than 300 people towards Yemen, the United Nations migration agency said on Sunday.The boat was carrying 305 people, most of them Ethiopians, when it sank near Guhere, off Djibouti’s eastern coast, in the Gulf of Aden during the night of October 8-9, according to the international organisation for migration (IOM). At least 82 people survived, all of them Ethiopian nationals.“Survivors told me that the boat started to sink backwards as soon as they got in it,” Alexandre Coissac, IOM’s chief of mission in Djibouti, said, describing the incident as a “devastating loss of life”.The agency initially reported 109 deaths and 116 people missing, but revised the toll to 139 dead and 84 missing after more bodies were recovered. The official count may rise further, as some bodies buried by migrants themselves have yet to be verified by authorities, Coissac told the Associated Press.Djiboutian authorities continued search and rescue operations, while IOM teams provided emergency assistance. The agency said it was assisting 64 survivors at a migrant centre in the coastal town of Obock.The crossing from the Horn of Africa to Yemen via the Bab al-Mandeb strait is a popular but dangerous route for migrants seeking jobs and safety in Gulf countries. The narrow waterway separates Djibouti and Yemen, but the journey carries significant risks amid conflict and instability across the region.“Poverty, insecurity and the growing impacts of climate change drive many to undertake this journey, despite mounting instability across the Middle East,” the IOM said.Coissac said 150 people aboard the boat had previously been turned back from Yemen but had attempted the crossing again.The agency recorded more than 20,000 incoming movements from Ethiopia to Djibouti since September 10. In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the sea route to Yemen, while the number attempting the journey rose by 18%, according to the IOM.The latest disaster follows a shipwreck in March 2026 that left nine people dead and 45 missing.IOM director general Amy Pope urged governments and donors to expand support for search and rescue operations and create safer migration routes.“No one gets into a boat like that unless they believe there is no other safe way,” Pope said. “We cannot keep treating these deaths as normal. Safe and legal pathways save lives.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Jennifer Garner’s work with organic children’s food has a connection to a place that has been part of her family’s life for generations.In Locust Grove, Oklahoma, a family farm that has been in Garner’s family since 1936 has helped shape her understanding of where food comes from and how children might develop a closer relationship with farming. Garner, who joined Once Upon a Farm as a co-founder in 2017, has spoken about the importance of making nutritious food more accessible to families. The business began with a practical problem: its original founders struggled to find the kind of organic baby food they wanted in local shops. Years later, the company has expanded across the United States, while Garner’s family farm remains a source of inspiration for its products.Garner’s family farm has been in Oklahoma since 1936The Oklahoma property has been in Garner’s family located in Locust Grove; it has remained more than a backdrop to the actress’s childhood memories. Her uncle Robert still lives there and manages the farm, preserving a connection between the land and the family’s everyday life.Garner has described, "Once I started working for Once Upon a Farm, I loved the idea of connecting kids to the farm early on. And so here we are, connecting kids to the farm and it gets to be my family’s farm that’s been with us since 1936. One thing that I love about the farm is that my Uncle Robert still lives here. He is the holder of the stories and runs the farm to this day."Once Upon a Farm has developed into a national brand, the family’s agricultural roots offer a more personal reference point for its emphasis on organic ingredients and childhood nutrition.How Garner joined the company behind organic children’s foodOnce Upon a Farm was founded in 2015 by Cassandra Curtis and Ari Raz. Curtis wanted better options for her daughter after finding that the baby food available in nearby supermarkets did not meet her expectations. She began developing recipes herself, eventually bringing cold-pressure-protected baby food to retail shelves.Garner became involved in 2017, alongside John Foraker, the former chief executive of organic food company Annie’s. Foraker brought experience in building and scaling a consumer food business, while Garner offered the perspective of a parent who had encountered similar questions about what to feed young children.The company’s range has since grown beyond its original baby food products. It now includes organic snacks, smoothies and meals for children at different stages, with products distributed through major retailers across the country. Once Upon a Farm has described its aim as making nutritious food easier for families to find and serve.The family farm behind Garner’s farm-to-food philosophyFor Garner, the connection between agriculture and childhood nutrition has been a recurring theme in her work with the company. Her family’s Oklahoma farm provides a tangible example of where food begins, rather than presenting it solely as a finished product on a supermarket shelf.In material published by Once Upon a Farm, Garner spoke about wanting children to develop an early connection with farming. The fact that her own family’s property has remained in use for decades gives that idea a personal dimension. Her uncle’s continued involvement also means that farming knowledge has not been separated from the place where it was acquired.Once Upon a Farm has built its range around organic produce and refrigerated products, distinguishing its approach from the shelf-stable baby food that has long occupied a large part of the market.Once Upon a Farm expands its reach while focusing on nutrition accessOnce Upon a Farm’s expansion has taken it well beyond its original retail footprint. By August 2026, Forbes reported that the company was selling more than 40 products in over 25,000 stores. Its portfolio had grown to include drinkable smoothies and oat bars, alongside food for babies and young children.As reported by Forbes, the company also entered the public markets in February 2026, with an initial public offering valued at approximately $724 million. Garner marked the occasion at the New York Stock Exchange, but told Forbes that she preferred to concentrate on the company’s operations rather than follow daily movements in its share price.She holds a reported 7% stake in the business and serves as chief brand officer. Her responsibilities have included working with retailers and helping communicate the company’s purpose to families. Forbes estimated her stake to be worth about $55 million in its August 2026 report, although the value of publicly traded shares can change.Access to nutritious food has also become part of the company’s work. Garner told Forbes that obtaining certification for the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children, commonly known as WIC, was a major priority. The programme helps eligible low-income families buy approved foods, and Once Upon a Farm had secured certification in more than 20 states by the time of the report.You use AI every day. articles.title: Buckingham Palace workers find 137-year-old theatre listings, 1966 newspaper pages and a sixpence ticket to a 1949 palace card game
articles.summary: Restoration work at Buckingham Palace has uncovered a collection of objects hidden beneath floorboards and inside the building’s infrastructure, with some
articles.body: Restoration work at Buckingham Palace has uncovered a collection of objects hidden beneath floorboards and inside the building’s infrastructure, with some items dating back to the 19th century. The discoveries include battered hobnailed boots, old newspaper pages, betting slips, theatre listings from 1889 and a ticket for a card game held at the palace in 1949.According to the BBC, workers also uncovered a typed document outlining Queen Elizabeth II’s arrangements for a diplomatic reception in 1977. The items came to light during a refurbishment aimed at replacing ageing cables, lead pipes, electrical wiring and boilers.Old newspaper pages and other items were found at Buckingham PalaceWorkers discovered several items during the refurbishment. These included a pair of battered black hobnailed boots, several betting slips, an empty Silk Cut cigarette carton and a bottle of Schweppes Still Malvern English Spring Water.Pages from a 1966 edition of the Daily Express were also among the items recovered. The newspaper carried an article about the Great Train Robbery and the prison where those convicted of the crime were held. Workers also recovered a pewter tankard, a wooden junction box and a faded box containing six Christmas cards.The objects are thought to have belonged to palace staff who worked there decades ago. Many had remained hidden beneath floorboards or within the building’s infrastructure.Historical items were found during Buckingham Palace restorationThe discoveries include a fragment of a theatre listing published in The Standard newspaper, now known as the Evening Standard, on 27 November 1889. Workers also recovered fragments of Minton decorative ceramic tiles from a fireplace hearth, with the design dating to around the mid-1800s.Among the items, there was a ticket for a whist drive, a card game event hosted by the Buckingham Palace social club on 14 April 1949. The ticket cost sixpence, or 6d, and dates to the reign of King George VI, King Charles III’s grandfather. The collection also contained blank Littlewoods Football Pool betting slips from 1957.Queen Elizabeth II’s diplomatic reception schedule uncovered at Buckingham PalaceA typed schedule detailing Queen Elizabeth II’s plans to host a diplomatic reception at Buckingham Palace in 1977 was among the recovered papers, dating to her Silver Jubilee year.The schedule revealed the monarch would work the room in a clockwise direction, and aides were asked to encourage the 350 British guests to mingle with the diplomats at the annual gathering.The schedule specified that British guests would be distributed throughout the State Rooms, except the Music Room and West Gallery, where they should be encouraged to talk to diplomats.Why is Buckingham Palace replacing its ageing cables and pipesThe refurbishment aims to replace ageing electrical cables, lead pipes, wiring and boilers amid concerns about fire and water damage. Many are set to be replaced for the first time in 60 years. Workers also found electrical wire covered with vulcanised Indian rubber cabling, which posed the greatest fire risk to the building.The palace prioritised this cabling for replacement when restoration work began. The 10-year refurbishment is funded through a temporary increase in the Sovereign Grant, which pays for the royal family’s official duties. King Charles III and Queen Camilla currently live at Clarence House and will not move into Buckingham Palace once the refurbishment is complete.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Robert Pether: Australian detained in Iraq for years on his way home
articles.summary: Engineer Robert Pether was jailed on fraud charges in 2021 though the UN said his detention was illegal.
articles.body:
Australian engineer Robert Pether has left Iraq five years after he was arrested and, according to the UN, arbitrarily detained.

The 51-year-old was jailed on fraud charges in 2021 alongside a colleague amid a contract dispute between the consulting firm he worked for and the Central Bank of Iraq.

The UN has said Pether's detention was illegal, and an international court has ruled his employer is not responsible for the business disagreement.

On Monday the Australian government confirmed Pether was on his way to being reunited with his family - who feared he would die in prison - at their home in Ireland.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the outcome followed "many years of persistent advocacy" by Australia and the Irish authorities.

"I spoke to Mr Pether shortly before his departure from Baghdad and am pleased he is now free to move forward with his life," she said.

"I'm hugely relieved," his wife Desree Pether told the BBC in a statement.

"It's been an absolute nightmare, especially these last few months. So many obstacles and plot twists right up to the last minute."

"We weren't going to say anything until he was safe at the end of his journey," she said, adding he was still in transit.

Pether was conditionally released from prison in Iraq last year, but barred from leaving the country, with Canberra at the time saying he continued to face the prospect of more legal proceedings.

Pether worked in the Middle East for almost a decade before taking on a huge rebuild of the Central Bank of Iraq's Baghdad headquarters in 2015.

He was arrested alongside his CME Consulting colleague, Egyptian Khalid Radwan, after the bank accused the men of stealing money from the project.

After being held without charge for almost six months, and then subjected to a speedy trial, the two were each given a five-year jail sentence and a joint fine of $12m (A$18.4m, £8.8m).

However, a 2022 report from the UN determined that the case contravened international law, and that Pether and Khalid had been subjected to "abusive and coercive" interrogations.

Iraq's government has previously denied allegations of ill treatment.

In 2023, the International Chamber of Commerce's (ICC) Court of Arbitration ruled that Iraq's central bank was at fault in the dispute with CME, and ordered it to pay $13m to the company.

articles.title: A battered 1677 wooden cabinet looked like an ordinary old box; one photograph of its original key helped Sotheby’s identify a rare piece that sold for $1.64 million
articles.summary: A small carved oak cabinet made in Salem, Massachusetts, in 1677 reached Sotheby’s as a few photographs submitted through its online portal.
articles.body: A small carved oak cabinet made in Salem, Massachusetts, in 1677 reached Sotheby’s as a few photographs submitted through its online portal. To an untrained eye, it might have looked like a grungy old box. Then Erik Gronning, a senior advisor in Sotheby’s American Furniture, Folk Art and Decorative Arts Department, saw the last image: the cabinet’s original key. It was, he says, the moment he knew for certain it was a period piece. In January 2026, the Symon and Rebeckah Horne Pilgrim Century Valuables Cabinet sold for $1,636,000, the highest price for American furniture in more than a decade.What made the battered 1677 wooden cabinet worth $1.64 millionAccording to Sotheby's, the piece is titled the Highly Important Symon and Rebeckah Horne Pilgrim Century Valuables Cabinet. It is attributed to the Symonds shops in Salem and dated 1677. Sotheby's records the sale price as $1,636,000. An untrained eye might read the object as a grungy old box. Sotheby's states that it is one of only five known examples attributed to the Symonds shops, and the only one to survive with its original key.The carved door bears the initials of Symon and Rebeckah Horne, an Andover couple, on either side of a small heart. Erik Gronning, a senior advisor in Sotheby's American Furniture, Folk Art and Decorative Arts Department, says the heart was included to symbolise the couple's love. Above it is the date the Hornes had the cabinet made: 1677, the year their son was born.How did the cabinet’s original key prove it was a rare 17th-century pieceThe submitted photographs included an image of the cabinet's original key. Gronning recalls his first reaction to the submission, saying, "I did not believe it was real when I saw it." He says it was the final submitted image, the one showing the original key, that made him certain the cabinet was a period piece and a highly important one.The cabinet to the Symonds shops and says it is the only one of the five known examples to retain its original key. In the account Sotheby's gives, a single photograph therefore moved the cabinet from an object that appeared ordinary to one that its specialist regarded as of high importance.Why did Sotheby’s sell the 1677 wooden cabinet for $1.64 million in 2026The cabinet descended through the Horne family for generations. It later passed to a local historical society, which the article says had quietly held it for some sixty years before deciding to let it go. The piece then came to Sotheby's through the submissions portal.The sale took place in 2026, and the final price was $1,636,000. The auction house describes this as the highest price for American furniture in more than ten years. Sotheby's presents the cabinet alongside four other portal submissions: a Ten Commandments tablet, a Claude Lalanne armchair, a Rolex Daytona and a Qianlong-period Chinese vase.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mumbai is already thirsty: Why the 2041 problem is really a 2026 problem
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Mumbai’s water crisis is not a problem to be pushed to the next decade.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Mumbai’s water crisis is not a problem to be pushed to the next decade. The city is already struggling with water scarcity, facing a 10% water cut and increasingly unpredictable monsoons, even as its demand is expected to soar 57% by 2041. The warning is stark: The infrastructure to ensure Mumbai’s future water supply is not keeping pace with the urgency of today.Demand has already outpaced supplyMumbai gets some 4,100 million liters of water per day (MLD) from seven lakes and dams, but its actual daily requirement is estimated at some 4,600-4,665 MLD, leaving a deficit of more than 500 MLD. The BMC’s environment status report 2025-26 expects demand to reach 6,424 MLD by 2041.That would leave a gap of 2,324 MLD against today’s supply, even without taking into account the challenge of sourcing additional sources and efficiently distributing water.The immediate crisis shows the vulnerability. Mumbai’s reservoirs did not fill to their full capacity by the end of the monsoon this year after deficient rainfall in August and September.In June, the water levels in the seven lakes dropped to less than 10% of their total capacity, and the BMC imposed stringent restrictions. By September, the stocks had recovered to around 96% but the civic administration went ahead with the 10% cut. The Maharashtra government has also ordered a minimum 10% cut in water supply in urban and rural areas from October 16 in view of the drought-like conditions.The key is three big projectsThe BMC has identified six more sources which are expected to contribute 3,303 MLD in total. Three projects – Gargai, Pinjal and Damanganga-Pinjal inter-state scheme – constitute 2,891 MLD, or about 88% of the proposed augmentation. But their progress illustrates how much more is required to get water from a source to household taps.Gargai, expected to supply 440 MLD, is under construction and is expected to be completed by 2029. The Pinjal, which is to contribute 865 MLD, is still in the planning stage while the 1,586 MLD Damanganga-Pinjal project is still on paper.This requires coordination between the Center and Maharashtra and Gujarat governments. The delays in these projects are important as Mumbai is unable to depend only on the seven existing reservoirs to bridge the growing supply gap.Desalination is an alternative, but not a quick fixIn addition, the BMC is also building two desalination plants at Manori and Versova with each having a capacity of 200 MLD and a 12 MLD advanced tertiary treatment plant at Colaba. Initial work on Manori has been started and the project is expected to add to the city’s sources apart from rain-dependent reservoirs. But even the first 200 MLD from Manori would only be a part of the present deficit of over 500 MLD.The real test is in executionThe issue came to the fore during a visit by mayor Ritu Tawde, standing committee chairman Prabhakar Shinde and other ruling BJP leaders to Tansa and Modak Sagar lakes. They pressed hydraulic engineering officials for details to speed up Pinjal and Damanganga-Pinjal. The challenge is not just announcing new sources but getting clearances, coordinating across governments and completing projects on time.By 2041, Mumbai’s demand is projected to be 56.7% higher than the existing supply of 4,100 MLD. But already, the city is short of water today.Unless long-pending projects shift from plans to reliable supply, the 2041 deadline risks becoming a false comfort: Mumbai will not suddenly face a water crisis in 2041. articles.title: China sanctions Paraguay, Belize ministers over diplomatic ties with Taiwan
articles.summary: China imposed sanctions on Paraguay’s communications minister and Belize’s foreign minister on Monday over their countries’ diplomatic ties with Taiwan,
articles.body: China imposed sanctions on Paraguay’s communications minister and Belize’s foreign minister on Monday over their countries’ diplomatic ties with Taiwan, which Beijing claims as part of its territory.The measures include restrictions on entry into mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, as well as a ban on Chinese organisations and individuals engaging in transactions, cooperation or other activities with the sanctioned officials, China’s foreign ministry said in separate notices.Beijing cited national sovereignty and security as the reasons for the sanctions, accusing some politicians in Belize and Paraguay of being "anti-China" for advocating continued diplomatic relations with Taiwan.Paraguay and Belize are among the 12 countries that maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan. China considers the self-governed island a province of its territory and opposes its recognition as a sovereign state. Taiwan’s government strongly rejects Beijing’s claim.The sanctions are largely symbolic, as officials from Taiwan’s diplomatic allies generally do not travel to China. Beijing has previously imposed similar measures on Western politicians over their support for Taiwan.Neither Paraguay’s Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies nor Belize’s foreign ministry immediately responded to requests for comment. Taiwan’s foreign ministry also had no immediate comment.The move follows recent diplomatic engagements between the countries and Taiwan. Belize Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca met his Taiwanese counterpart, Lin Chia-lung, in Belize last month. In June, Paraguay’s Minister of Information and Communication Technologies, Gustavo Villate, met Taiwan Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi in Paraguay.China has stepped up efforts to persuade Taiwan’s remaining diplomatic partners to sever formal ties with Taipei and recognise Beijing instead.The most recent country to switch diplomatic recognition from Taiwan to China was the Pacific island nation of Nauru in 2024. Honduras ended its decades-long diplomatic relationship with Taiwan in 2023.Beijing maintains that Taiwan is an inseparable part of China and has not ruled out the use of force to bring the island under its control. Taiwan, which has its own democratically elected government and military, maintains that its future can be decided only by its people.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Bradford children cut down on social media screen time for trial
articles.summary: Researchers say it is the first major study into the impact of social media on teens' mental health.
articles.body:
Thousands of teenagers have joined a trial to limit their time on social media as part of a major study.

Researchers at Born in Bradford believe the IRL (In Real Life) trial is the first major scientific study into the impact of limiting social media on young people's mental health.

Results from the study will help inform how the government implements a social media ban for under-16s that was announced in May and would be introduced by spring 2027.

During preliminary stages, 200 students aged 12-15 were asked to limit social media use, but now the research team has recruited 4,000 students from Bradford secondary schools.

Dawson, 12, is one of the students taking part. He said he spent about two hours a day on social media and was looking forward to spending less time on his smartphone.

"I think it will make stronger relationships because I won't be on my phone as much," he said.

"I feel like I spend too much on it and I don't think I focus on the things I should."

His dad, Adam, said he hoped the trial would allow him to spend more time with his son.

"I might see more of him downstairs, that would be a good start.

"If he's not always on his phone, he can be out seeing his friends more. It will be a challenge, but I hope he'll get there."

Some students will use a smartphone app that limits their social media use, while others will carry on as normal, without any limitations.

At the start and end of the six-week period, participants will be asked to fill in short questionnaires about how they are feeling - covering things like anxiety, sleep, body image and school life.

At Appleton Academy in Wyke, where many of the students have been recruited, Hannah, 12, Blossom, 13, and Louis, 12, said they would miss communicating with friends on social media.

"A lot of people spend a lot of time on social media and they have friends there so it would be sad if screen time was only two hours," said Hannah.

"I think it will be hard for the first two weeks but over time we should get used to it," added Louis.

Rachel Garlick, Head of Secondary at Appleton Academy, said it was important to get the children's opinions on the impact a ban might have for them.

"It's really important we allow them to have that voice," she said.

"They rely on social media such a lot for all their communication with each other."

Dr John Pickavance, trial manager, said the study would create "rigorous scientific" evidence for future policy making.

"The government has made that decision but we don't have any details yet and we don't know how it's going to be implemented," he said.

"We want there to be the best evidence available to any policy makers, now or in the future, so these decisions are being made in the young people's best interests."

articles.title: Kolhapur man 'pushes' girlfriend into 1,000ft-deep valley after her family fixes marriage elsewhere
articles.summary: KOLHAPUR: A family’s decision to get their daughter married elsewhere allegedly led to the murder of a 23-year-old engineering student, whose boyfriend is
articles.body: KOLHAPUR: A family’s decision to get their daughter married elsewhere allegedly led to the murder of a 23-year-old engineering student, whose boyfriend is accused of pushing her into a nearly 1,000ft-deep valley in Kolhapur district.Tarrannum Naik, a third-year engineering student from Gargoti, was found dead in the valley below Naikwadi waterfall in Bhudargad taluka.Her boyfriend, Sripad Vadar, 25, was arrested on Sunday after police found inconsistencies in his account of the circumstances leading to her death.Tarrannum’s marriage had been fixed for November 12, locals said. Vadar, who works with his brother, a local contractor, allegedly told police that he and Tarrannum had been in a relationship for five-and-a-half years and had decided to die by suicide together after her family arranged her marriage to another man.The case surfaced on Saturday morning when Vadar approached a police station and reported that Tarrannum had fallen into the valley from a cliff. He claimed she jumped but that he lost his nerve at the last moment.Police initially registered a case under Section 140(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to wrongful confinement. However, an examination of the couple’s chat history cast doubt on his account of a suicide pact.“The chat history does not support the account he gave us about a suicide pact. The messages suggested Sripad was upset over Tarrannum’s family’s decision to get her married to someone else. That raised serious doubts and led us to invoke BNS section 103(1) for murder,” said Vivek Patil, sub-divisional police officer, Gadhinglaj.Police are awaiting the postmortem report to determine whether Tarrannum jumped or was pushed into the valley. Patil said an advanced analysis of the report was expected to take three to four days.A local court on Sunday remanded Vadar in five days of police custody. Police have seized the mobile phones of both for forensic analysis.Naikwadi waterfall lies in an isolated, forested area about 50km from Gargoti. The waterfall had dried up after the monsoon, and there were no visitors at the spot when the couple reached there on Friday, police said.The alleged murder triggered outrage in Gargoti, where residents marched to the police station on Sunday demanding a fast-track trial.Locals said Tarrannum lived with her maternal grandmother in the Shivajinagar area of Gargoti while pursuing her studies and returned home during vacations.
